items.followUp: Explain alcoholic fermentation and name its end products.

rubric.why: Identifies glucose as the substance broken down and the absence of oxygen during the process.
rubric.description: Lactic acid fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down without oxygen.

rubric.why: Identifies lactic acid as the product and recognises that energy is released or that lactic acid is formed from pyruvic acid.
rubric.description: The process forms lactic acid and releases a small amount of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lactic acid as a product and stating that energy is released, or for describing its formation from pyruvic acid.

modelAnswer: Lactic acid fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose in muscle cells or some bacteria.
It forms lactic acid and releases a small amount of energy (about 2 ATP per glucose molecule).

items.followUp: Explain how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: States that increasing carbon dioxide concentration raises the photosynthesis rate while carbon dioxide is limiting.
rubric.description: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis while carbon dioxide is a limiting factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased carbon dioxide concentration to an increased rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Recognises that the rate eventually stops increasing because another factor limits photosynthesis.
rubric.description: At a high enough concentration, the rate levels off because another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate levels off or stops increasing at high carbon dioxide concentration.

modelAnswer: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis while carbon dioxide is a limiting factor.
At a high enough concentration, the rate levels off because another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: Define biology and describe the contributions of two Muslim scientists to biology.

rubric.description: Biology is the study of life or living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of biology.

rubric.why: Names Al-Asmai and identifies his work on animals.
rubric.description: Abdul Malik Al-Asmai studied animals and wrote books about them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Al-Asmai and describing his work on animals.

rubric.why: Names Ibn Sina and gives a relevant contribution to medicine.
rubric.description: Ibn Sina was a famous physician and wrote Al-Qanun fit-Tibb, an important medical work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Ibn Sina and stating a relevant medical contribution or naming his medical work.

rubric.why: Names Jabir bin Hayyan and identifies his biological writings.
rubric.description: Jabir bin Hayyan also wrote works on animals and plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Jabir and identifying his writings on animals or plants.

modelAnswer: Biology is the study of life and living organisms.
Abdul Malik Al-Asmai studied animals and wrote books about them.
Ibn Sina was a famous physician and wrote Al-Qanun fit-Tibb, an important medical work.
Jabir bin Hayyan also wrote works on animals and plants.

items.followUp: Define enzymes and explain how temperature and substrate specificity affect their action.

rubric.why: Defines enzymes by their role in speeding up chemical reactions in living organisms.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining enzymes as biological catalysts.

rubric.why: States the protein nature of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: Describes the specificity of enzyme action.
rubric.description: Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme acts on a particular substrate or reaction.

rubric.why: Gives a further characteristic, such as reusability or the effect of conditions on enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Enzymes remain unchanged after reactions and can be reused; their activity is affected by temperature and pH, and extreme conditions can denature them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct further characteristic of enzymes.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
An enzyme remains unchanged after a reaction and can be used again; its activity is affected by temperature and pH, and extreme conditions can denature it.
